## Summary

I diagnosed the `js-crdt-orset-epoch-compaction-causal-resurrection` class and implemented a verified deterministic CRDT repair tool.

**Root cause:** reclaiming tombstones with ephemeral removal records causes causal resurrection (stale/out-of-order adds replay a dropped tag), unsafe compaction (folding before all replicas ack), and epoch-rollover regressions (churn lowers the stable frontier).

**The fix — monotonic causal watermark:**
- Remove ops carry a causal `context` (origin version vector); a dot dominated by it is dead (remove-wins).
- Tombstones fold into a per-value **watermark** only when `remove.dot <= stable`, where `stable` is the component-wise min of active members' acknowledged VVs.
- `stable` is `max`-ed with its previous value, so joins (counter 0) and leaves can never un-prove a compacted tombstone.
- Adds are checked against the watermark **at integration time**, so they can never be stored then resurrect.
- Epoch only increments on real folds; watermark survives rollover.
- Replayed compacted adds are rejected with a **minimal replay witness** (the single remove op + dominating watermark entry).

**Files:**
- `crdt-repair.js` — implementation
- `test-crdt-repair.js` — 12 assertions, all passing
- `fuzz.js` — 200-trial randomized convergence, passing
- `SOLUTION.md` — full write-up with title, root-cause analysis, embedded code, verification results, and a requirement→test coverage map

Verification output: `12 tests passed` and `fuzz OK: 200 trials converged`.
